History and Physical (H&P – Super Detailed)

Consult Summary:
• 40-year-old woman with 6-day history of dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, and microscopic-appearing hematuria; no fever or flank pain. Clinical impression is an uncomplicated lower urinary tract infection; empiric 3-day oral antibiotic prescribed via telehealth.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Pain on urination.
• Onset/duration: Began 6 days ago; ongoing.
• Character/progression:
  – Dysuria each time she voids.
  – Foul-smelling urine.
  – Intermittent lower central abdominal pain, rated 7/10, comes and goes.
  – Small “spots” of blood noted in urine over same 6-day period.
• Associated symptoms:
  – Denies fever/temperature changes.
  – Denies flank or loin pain.
  – Denies difficulty initiating stream or urinary retention.
  – Denies vaginal discharge.
  – Eating and drinking normally.
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None identified.
• Menstrual history: Regular menses.
• Review of systems (pertinent negatives): No back pain, no weight loss, no change in bowel habit beyond baseline IBS, no other systemic symptoms reported.

Past Medical History:
• Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) – currently stable; no recent flare noted.
• No prior urinary tract infections or renal disease reported.
• No past surgeries reported.
• Medications:
  – Mebeverine 200 mg three times daily (regular use).
• Drug allergies:
  – Clindamycin (reaction details not documented).

Social History:
• Lives with friends.
• Occupation: Support worker.
• Alcohol: ~1 glass of wine per week.
• Smoking: Never smoker.
• Recreational drugs: Not mentioned.
• Sexual history: No recent increase in sexual activity reported.

Family History:
• Denies significant family medical conditions (specifics not provided).

Physical Examination:
• Telehealth visit – no in-person examination performed.
• Vitals: Not obtained.

Investigations:
• None performed; empiric treatment initiated without urinalysis per guideline for uncomplicated cystitis.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1 – Dysuria / Suspected Acute Uncomplicated Cystitis
  • Assessment: 6-day history of dysuria, malodorous urine, suprapubic pain, and microscopic hematuria without systemic features → likely lower urinary tract infection.
  • Plan:
    – Prescribe 3-day course of oral antibiotic (exact drug/dose not documented).
    – Send electronic prescription to patient’s nominated pharmacy (Knightsbridge Pharmacy); advise pick-up within ~1 hour.
    – Hydration: Encourage 2.5–3 L water daily.
    – Adjuncts: Consider cranberry juice; OTC urinary alkalinizing sachets (details to be added to patient notes).
    – Monitoring: Purchase thermometer; check temperature periodically.
    – Safety-net: Seek medical review if pain worsens, new flank/back pain, fever, difficulty voiding, or recurrence of symptoms after treatment.

Issue 2 – IBS (history, currently quiescent)
  • Assessment: Stable on current regimen.
  • Plan: Continue Mebeverine 200 mg TID.

Issue 3 – Drug allergy
  • Assessment: Clindamycin allergy.
  • Plan: Document prominently; avoid clindamycin in future prescribing.

General plan items
  • No routine follow-up required if symptoms resolve; advised to re-consult if no improvement or recurrent episodes.

Quality checks (document_quality):
• Expected but missing: Objective vitals, urinalysis, pregnancy status, detailed clindamycin reaction, comprehensive medication list (only Mebeverine documented).
• Internal conflicts: None noted.
• Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional minor interruptions but clinically adequate.
